correctness.rationale: All three signed dot-product inequalities were independently matched to the ordered horizontal gaps s,t and ordinate differences. The middle horizontal vertex must be a strict vertical extreme, with 0<st/epsilon²<AB and a branch-dependent lower threshold. For the s<t branch put z=st/epsilon², t>constant*epsilon; the threshold error is O(epsilon²/t²) and the resulting integral produces epsilon² dt/t. Bounded-variation translation controls f(x)f(x+s)f(x+s+t) versus f(x)^3 by O(s+t). The exact six-permutation identity, including tied heights, has E[1_{middle strict extreme} A min(A,B)]=Var(Y), independently checked on triples with and without ties. Hence two equal logarithmic branches contribute 6v int f³ each. The common-measure change-of-variables density and matching total masses permit Scheffé to prove total-variation convergence, not just weak convergence; Jensen yields sharp int f³>=L^-2 with uniform equality. Numerical Bernoulli and Monte Carlo diagnostics are not an infinite proof.
